reasons.A: Short, plain declaratives with a dry understated turn ('slow learners at that', 'He is only a schoolboy') match the passage's earnest-but-wry movement and its unfussy period diction.
reasons.B: Right period register and gentle irony, but the long cumulative sentences, semicolons and elaborate letter-in-the-post conceit are more ornate and witty than the passage's plainer rhythm.
reasons.C: The 'first part / second part / third part' scaffolding and modern words ('flawed', 'blind spots') read as a present-day explainer, not the author's plain period voice.
